2609.20068.title: Marginal utility, matrix factorization, and the Key-Value (KV) cache: a unified information-economic framework for sovereign geo-mining inference
2609.20068.paper_summary: This paper builds a theoretical bridge between the economic notion of marginal utility and two machine-learning constructs, matrix factorization and the Key--Value cache of transformer language models. The singular value spectrum of a rating matrix is shown to be a diminishing marginal utility schedule for latent factors, the eigenvalue spectrum of the projected covariance operator to be the marginal utility schedule of a model's learned representation, and cache eviction and low-rank cache compression to be instances of constrained utility maximization under a memory budget. The three collapse into a single allocation rule: retain the top dimensions whose eigenvalue exceeds the shadow price of the binding constraint. The framework is applied to the automated extraction of structured information from geo-mining documents, where it motivates a multi-pass inference protocol, a layer-wise TIES model merging procedure, and a selection policy combining extraction quality, localization drift and energy, scalarized with a Conditional Value-at-Risk term on drift. Two empirical contributions are reported. An 11.2-million-parameter hierarchical classifier, trained in about five minutes on a single GPU, reaches 90.0 per cent level-1 accuracy on a held-out test set from a 973-document uranium-exploration corpus, against 92.0 per cent for a proprietary model on a fifty-document human audit of the same corpus, at a latency of 2.62 ms per card against approximately 2,000 ms for the API and at negligible cost. A diagnostic of uniform-density TIES merging exposes a reproducible degenerate mode in which the merged model returns token-identical outputs across five geographically distinct districts while declaring high confidence; re-executing the merge under layer-wise calibrated densities removes that signature on the diagnostic sample. The full-scale extraction benchmark, including LoRA fine-tuning, is reported as projected rather than measured and remains an empirical extension of this work.
2609.20068.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文建立了一個理論橋樑，將邊際效用的經濟概念與兩個機器學習構造——矩陣分解和Transformer語言模型的鍵值快取——聯繫起來。評分矩陣的奇異值譜被顯示為潛在因素的邊際效用時間表，投影協方差運算子的特徵值譜則是模型學習表示的邊際效用時間表，而快取驅逐和低秩快取壓縮則是受限效用最大化在記憶預算下的實例。這三者合併為一個單一的分配規則：保留特徵值超過約束條件影子價格的頂部維度。該框架應用於從地質挖掘文件中自動提取結構化信息，並促進了一個多次推理協議、一個層級 TIES 模型合併程序，以及一個結合提取質量、定位漂移和能量的選擇政策，並在漂移上用條件風險價值項進行標量化。報告了兩項實證貢獻。一個擁有 1120 萬參數的層級分類器，在單個 GPU 上訓練約五分鐘，達到了在 973 份鈾勘探文檔的保留測試集上 90.0% 的一級準確率，而對於同一語料庫的 50 份文檔的人類審核，專有模型的準確率為 92.0%，每張卡的延遲為 2.62 毫秒，相較於 API 的約 2000 毫秒，且成本微乎其微。對均勻密度 TIES 合併的診斷揭示了一種可重現的退化模式，在該模式下，合併模型在五個地理上不同的區域返回相同的標記輸出，同時聲稱高置信度；在層級校準密度下重新執行合併則消除了該診斷樣本上的特徵。全規模提取基準，包括 LoRA 微調，報告為預測而非測量，並仍然是這項工作的實證擴展。
2609.20068.author: Caroline Gans Combe et.al.
